2. By order dated 15.6.2024 in Petition No. 108/TL/2024, Pachora Power
Transmission Limited (PPTL) was granted an inter-State transmission licence bearing
Licence No. 128/Transmission/2024/CERC, for the establishment of the Transmission
system for Evacuation of Power from RE Projects in Rajgarh (1000 MW) SEZ in
Madhya Pradesh-Phase II.
3. The Petitioner has submitted that an application under Section 14(1) of the
Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 41 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014
was filed before the Regional Director (WR), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Mumbai,
seeking approval for the conversion of the company into a Private Limited Company,
which was duly approved vide Order dated 26.5.2026 by the Regional Director.
Thereafter, the Regional Director sanctioned the alteration of Clause I of the
Memorandum of Association, from “Pachora Power Transmission Limited” to “Pachora
Power Transmission Private Limited”.
4. Subsequently, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs also issued a Certificate of
Incorporation dated 30.6.2026 consequent upon conversion to a private company,
duly recording the aforesaid conversion.
5. The Petitioner has submitted that, consequent to the change in name of the
transmission licensee, there has been no change in the composition or structure of the
company.
Analysis and Decision
6. This Petition is being decided by way of circulation.
Order in Petition No. 571/RC/2026 Page 5

7. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and perused the
documents available on record. The Petitioner was granted the transmission licence
vide order dated 15.6.2024 in Petition No. 108/TL/2024.
8. Consequent to the issuance of the certificate dated 30.6.2026 by the Ministry of
Corporate Affairs, as noted above, we direct that the name of the Transmission
Licensee be changed from “Pachora Power Transmission Limited” to “Pachora Power
Transmission Private Limited” in the records of the Commission. It is further stipulated
that Pachora Power Transmission Private Limited shall remain unequivocally bound by
the terms and conditions of the inter-State transmission licence originally granted to
Pachora Power Transmission Limited, provisions of the Transmission Service
Agreement, Transmission Licence Regulations, and the Electricity Act, 2003.
9. We direct that the necessary endorsement be made on the transmission licence
with regard to the change of name of “Pachora Power Transmission Limited” to
“Pachora Power Transmission Private Limited”. Except for the name, there shall be no
change in the terms and conditions of the licence.
10. Let an extract copy of this order be sent to the Central Government (the
Ministry of Power), the Central Electricity Authority, and the Central Transmission
Utility of India Limited in terms of sub-section (7) of Section 15 of the Electricity Act,
2003, for their information and record.
11. Accordingly, Petition No. 571/RC/2026 is allowed in terms of the above.

ORDER
The Petitioner, Bijapur REZ Transmission Limited (now known as Bijapur REZ
Transmission Private Limited), has filed the present Regulatory Compliance
Application seeking approval to change the name of the Transmission Licensee from
“Bijapur REZ Transmission Limited” To “Bijapur REZ Transmission Private Limited”.
The Petitioner has made the following prayer:
“(a) Allow the present petition;
(b) Take on record the change in name of the transmission licensee/
Petitioner from “Bijapur REZ Transmission Limited” to “Bijapur REZ
Transmission Private Limited”, in terms as stated in the present Petition;
(c) Direct that necessary endorsement be made on the transmission licensee
with regard to change of name of “Bijapur REZ Transmission Limited” to
“Bijapur REZ Transmission Private Limited”;

Petitioner on account of the above name change; and

deem fit in the interest of equity and justice.”

which was duly approved vide Order dated 26.5.2026 by the Regional Director.
Thereafter, the Regional Director sanctioned the alteration of Clause I of the
Memorandum of Association, i.e. “Bijapur REZ Transmission Limited” to “Bijapur REZ

The Petitioner, Assam Power Generation Corporation Limited, a Company
incorporated under Companies Act, has made the present application under Sections
14 and 15 (1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”) read with
Regulation 6 (1) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms

7. Clause (9) of Regulation 6 of the Trading Licence Regulations provides as under:
“(9) On consideration of further objections or suggestions received and the reply
of the applicant thereto, if any, the Commission may grant the licence or reject
the application, for reasons to be recorded in writing if the application does not
confirm to the provisions of the Act, the rules or regulations or provisions of any
other law for the time being in force:
Provided that no application shall be rejected, unless the applicant has been
given an opportunity of being heard.”
8. On consideration of the materials on record, we are satisfied that the Petitioner
company meets the requirements of the Act and the Trading Licence Regulations for
the grant of an inter-State trading licence for Category 'II'.
9. The grant of the trading licence to the Petitioner (hereinafter referred to as “the
licensee”) is subject to the fulfilment of the following conditions throughout the period

force;
(b) The licensee shall comply with orders and directions issued by the
Commission from time to time;
(c) The licensee shall not engage in the business of transmission of
electricity during the period of subsistence of the trading licence, i.e., till 25
years;
(d) The licensee shall charge trading margin strictly in accordance with the

(f) The licensee shall continue to be governed by the qualifications and
disqualifications specified in Chapter 2 of the Trading Licence Regulations
during the subsistence of the licence;
(g) The licensee shall continue to abide by the terms and conditions of the

(h) The licensee shall regularly pay the annual licence fee in accordance

आदेश/ ORDER
The Petitioner, Captive Power Producers Association (CPPA), is an association of
industries in Maharashtra and Gujarat. The members of the Petitioner Association have
installed captive generation plants in their industries in these states and meet their energy
requirements through captive-produced power. These captive power plants of the Petitioner
are recognised as ‘co-generation’ plants under the Electricity Act, 2003.
2. The Respondent, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), is a Ministry of the
Government of India. The salutary objective of MNRE is to develop and deploy new and
renewable energy to supplement the Country's energy requirements.
3. The present petition is filed by the Petitioner, CPPA, seeking revision in the methodology
evolved by the Commission vide its order dated 18.02.2020 in Suo Motu Petition No.
12/SM/2019 for estimation of electricity generated from biomass in a co-generation power
plant.
4. Petitioner has made the following prayers:

submissions. In this regard, reliance was placed on the judgments of the Supreme Court in
UPPCL v. NTPC Ltd., (2009) 6 SCC 235, to submit that the Commission has the power
to modify/ revisit the methodology and on the judgment of the APTEL in Ratnagiri Gas
and Power Private Ltd. v. CERC, 2011 SCC Appeal No. 130 of 2009, where it was held
that the Commission has the power to relax and modify when a Regulation in its
application leads to injustice and undue hardship. The Commission also relied on the
judgment of the APTEL in NTPC Ltd. v. AP Transmission Co. Ltd., wherein it was
submitted that where reasonable grounds exist to revisit an order, the Commission ought
to do so.
Analysis and Decision
14. The Commission has heard the counsel for the Petitioner and considered the submissions,
and has carefully perused the records. The Commission also notes that no one appeared
on behalf of the Respondent during the hearing, nor did they make any written
submissions in the matter.
15. Brief facts of the case: The Commission, vide its Order dated 18.02.2020 in Petition No.
12/SM/2019, specified the methodology for estimating the energy generated from
biomass in biomass co-fired coal-based thermal power plants, including captive power
plants and co-generation plants, which continues to be in force. As per the Petitioner
(CPPA), the Commission, in the said Order, recognised that in conventional coal-based
power plants, the entire heat generated from coal and biomass is used to generate power.
However, in co-generation plants, only part of the heat is used to generate power. Under
these circumstances, the Petitioner submitted that the methodology needs to be revisited
in light of the data available for the past three years, which demonstrated that it is not
suitable for co-generation plants, as it created inequality of treatment and unequal
benefits for RPO compliance. Therefore, the Petitioner suggested a methodology and
sought revision of the said methodology for estimating electricity generated from biomass
in biomass co-fired thermal power plants, particularly in respect of co-generation plants.
16. The Commission notes that the only issue that arises for consideration is whether the
methodology specified by the Commission vide its Order dated 18.02.2020 in Suo Motu
Petition No. 12/SM/2019 for estimation of electricity generated from biomass in
Order in Petition No. 110/MP/2024 Page 7 of 9

20. Further, as per the contention of the Petitioner that the methodology specified by the
Commission vide Order dated 18.02.2020 should be revisited on the basis of data
available for the past three years, the Commission notes that the Petitioner has not placed
on record any data covering the said three-year period. The Petitioner has furnished an
illustration supporting its suggested methodology for estimating the energy generated
from biomass in co-generation plants, based on one month’s actual data from one of its
members’ co-generation plants. However, such illustration does not, by itself, establish
that the methodology specified vide Order dated 18.02.2020 is inappropriate for co-
generation plants or warrants revision.
21. The Petitioner has also relied upon a catena of judicial decisions and contended that the
Commission possesses regulatory power to revisit its earlier determination. The
Commission recognises that it may revisit a methodology where the material placed on
record warrants such reconsideration. In the present case, as noted above, the
Commission already considered the specific distinction concerning co-generation plants
while framing the methodology in the Order dated 18.02.2020. Accordingly, the
Commission finds no sufficient basis to deviate from the methodology specified in the
said Order.
22. The prayers of the Petitioner in the instant Petition are, therefore, rejected.
23. Petition No. 110/MP/2024 is disposed of in terms of the above.
